concurrency_and_state: ResultSetImpl holds mutable cursor state (indexData initialized to -1) and mutable backing collections (Map<String, Object>[] data, Object[][] values) without synchronization; safe only for single-threaded per-query usage.
dispose() and close() clear row maps and null out data/values references; subsequent navigation/getter calls throw Exception("No data available") except gotoBeforeFirst() and getRows().
cross_module_questions: How do AlyraManager / callers invoke ResultSetImpl and close the underlying JDBC Connection when ResultSetImpl closes rs and stmt = rs.getStatement() in its finally block?

Do any SQL queries across DAO/fetcher classes rely on SELECT column aliases (e.g., COUNT(*) AS total) or MySQL 8.x DATETIME columns (which return java.time.LocalDateTime from rs.getObject(j)) when reading through ResultSetImpl?

db_redis_touchpoints.op: JDBC ResultSet consumption & resource cleanup (rs.close(), rs.getStatement().close())
db_redis_touchpoints.safety_note: Closes rs and stmt in finally, does not close Connection (assumed managed by caller); buffers all rows in memory; uses getColumnName() instead of getColumnLabel().

findings.impact: Any SQL query using column aliases (e.g., SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt) or computed expressions fails lookup by alias name via get*(String) and may return 0/null or overwrite keys.
findings.root_cause: ResultSetImpl constructor calls rsmd.getColumnName(j) instead of rsmd.getColumnLabel(j) when populating rowMap keys.
findings.title: getColumnName used instead of getColumnLabel breaks SQL aliases

findings.impact: Calling getTimestamp() on a DATETIME column in MySQL Connector/J 8.x throws Exception("Cannot convert LocalDateTime to Timestamp") at runtime.
findings.root_cause: Constructor extracts column values via rs.getObject(j) (which returns java.time.LocalDateTime for DATETIME in MySQL 8.x), while getTimestamp(int/String) only handles Timestamp, java.util.Date, and Long.
findings.title: getTimestamp fails on MySQL 8.x LocalDateTime from rs.getObject

findings.impact: Large query results cause high heap allocation, duplicate object references, and GC pauses.
findings.root_cause: Constructor eagerly buffers all rows into both List<Map<String, Object>> (one HashMap per row with column and table.column String keys) and List<Object[]> before closing ResultSet.
findings.title: Eager dual-structure in-memory buffering of entire ResultSet

findings.impact: Values exceeding int/short/byte bounds (e.g., BIGINT/long stats, currency, or quantities) silently wrap/truncate instead of throwing, risking stat or currency corruption.
findings.root_cause: getByte, getShort, and getInt cast any Number and call byteValue()/shortValue()/intValue() without range checking.
findings.title: Silent numeric truncation in getByte/getShort/getInt on Number values

findings.impact: Invalid column index throws raw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException; null column name throws raw NullPointerException; maintenance risk from 18 nearly identical getter implementations.
findings.root_cause: Indexed getters do not validate column bounds (1..nColumn) before indexing values[indexData][column - 1], string getters call column.toLowerCase() without null check, and cursor/conversion logic is duplicated across 18 getter methods.
findings.title: Missing column index/null validation and heavy boilerplate duplication across getters

key_classes.name: ResultSetImpl
key_classes.responsibility: Disconnected in-memory implementation of AlyraResultSet that copies a JDBC ResultSet into row maps and Object arrays, closes ResultSet/Statement, and provides typed cursor-based getters.

module_summary: ResultSetImpl (591 lines) implements AlyraResultSet as an eagerly buffered, disconnected JDBC ResultSet wrapper. Its constructor copies every row into both a case-insensitive HashMap (indexed by column name and table.column) and an Object[] array, then closes the JDBC ResultSet and Statement in a finally block before exposing cursor navigation and typed getters.
